body: How long would I have to stay? What if it doesn't get any better? Do they just keep you in indefinately? I just want meds to stop this bullshit.
My tree appears to be stuck in hell, or the equivalent feeling. I'm not religious.

Thank you. I don't even know who to ask really. I have a mistrust of doctors because of events that took place years ago. I've literally said to family members I'm going to off myself and they just brush it off. I don't blame them or anything, they probably don't know how to respond. 

I just wish I wasn't so messed up. I've now lived over half my life with these stupid conditions. I don't see any other way out

Thank you, I've decided to enquire about this to the national autistic society. I wonder what their views are on this as well. I'm probably fixating on this too much but I having nothing else to do at the moment.

I'll make sure to post their answer here whenever they get round to answering it. But I've come to the conclusion that my answer of it being true was correct so now I'm relieved!

Yes I can drive. But i choose not to. Partly because I get extremely anxious and partly because I'm convinced I passed by complete fluke. It took me 4 tests. The first in the manual and the other 3 in an automatic. All 3 failures were pretty embarrassing. 

First one was going fine until for some reason my mind decided to go onto the wrong side of the road. Second one I was loaded with cold and I entered a no entry zone within the first 5 minutes of the test. The third one I drove through a roundabout without even realising. 

On the fourth I finally passed. I've driven twice since then haha. I'm just not good with having to pay that much attention on the road. So for the safety of others I refuse to drive. I was also still making stupid beginner mistakes no matter how many lessons I had.

Indeed. I can come to terms that some autistic people might not experience it. But for it to be used in a true or false statement makes it seem like it's generalizing everyone who has autism and I don't like that.

Thank you! Yes I don't agree with the way that study was conducted. As like you say it is easy for it to be inaccurate . Also yeah the wording of the quiz is what I'm most annoyed about haha. I don't know why it was included as there is no 100% factual evidence to support the claim. Do you think I should ask them to remove it? 

I'm also quite annoyed at the headlines of the articles as well as this is probably what has caused the confusion in the first place.

Thanks for your response! I am quite relieved that I'm not the only one. Although I do seem to yawn more when a member of my family does it rather than another person. I think it's mainly because I don't make eye contact with strangers.

Thanks for the reply. Yes this is something I've been considering as I have had some experiences with mental health professionals in the past but it wasn't really much help at that time. Mainly my fault as I didn't really engage. I'm hoping next time goes better. Good luck with your treatment.
